title: Self-harm: psychosocial assessment
stem: Observation ward. Miss Peters, 24, was admitted overnight after taking 30 paracetamol and some sleeping tablets. Her 4-hour paracetamol level was below the treatment line and all her bloods are normal. She wants to go home. Assess her before discharge.

phases.title: Psychosocial assessment
phases.goal: The act, now, and the background.

phases.title: Agree a plan
phases.goal: A safety plan and follow-up, together.

review.text: SAD PERSONS. Your notes build the assessment around the score. NICE NG225 says not to use risk tools to predict repetition or suicide, or to decide who is treated or discharged. Do a psychosocial assessment: the act, current intent, mental illness, substances, previous self-harm, supports, protective factors, safeguarding, then a safety plan and follow-up.

notes:
Checked against NICE NG225 (Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence, 2022), NICE QS34, and HA guidance on suicide risk.

NICE NG225: do not use risk assessment tools and scales (such as SAD PERSONS) to predict future suicide or repetition, or to decide who is offered treatment or discharged. Do a psychosocial assessment: the act (method, planning, precautions against discovery, final acts, whether she expected to die, how she feels now it failed), current suicidal ideation and plans, mental illness, alcohol and drugs, previous self-harm, social circumstances and supports, protective factors, safeguarding (children at home, domestic abuse), and needs. Agree a safety plan, involve family if she consents, and arrange follow-up (psychiatry/crisis team).

Your notes build the station around the SAD PERSONS score; its items remain useful prompts, but the score itself should not drive the decision. The rest of your marking scheme (history, psychiatric, drug and social history, sensitive questioning, a plan) matches.

steps.label: Psychosocial assessment
steps.hint: The act, intent now, mental health, alcohol/drugs, previous self-harm, supports, protective factors, safeguarding.

The act.t: Can you tell me what happened last night?
The act.tz: 你可唔可以話我知，琴晚發生咩事？
The act.rz: 我同男朋友分咗手。我將櫃入面所有藥都食晒。
The act.r: I broke up with my boyfriend. I took everything in the cupboard.
The act.mark: Opens gently and asks about the event

The act.t: Had you planned it? Did you leave a note or do anything to prepare?
The act.tz: 你之前有冇計劃過？有冇留遺書，或者做過咩準備？
The act.rz: 冇，十分鐘內嘅事。冇留遺書。
The act.r: No, it was all in 10 minutes. No note.
The act.mark: Asks about planning and final acts

The act.t: What did you think would happen? Who found you?
The act.tz: 你嗰陣諗住會點？邊個發現你？
The act.rz: 我想瞓咗之後唔好再醒……之後我驚咗，打電話俾家姐。
The act.r: I wanted to sleep and not wake up… then I got scared and called my sister.
The act.mark: Asks about intent and whether she sought help

The act.t: How do you feel now that you're still here?
The act.tz: 你而家仲喺度，心入面覺得點？
The act.rz: 老實講，鬆咗一口氣。又覺得好尷尬。
The act.mark: Asks how she feels about surviving

Now.t: Are you thinking of harming yourself now?
Now.tz: 你而家有冇諗住傷害自己？
Now.r: No. I want to go home to my sister's.

Now.t: Mood, sleep, appetite over recent weeks?
Now.tz: 最近幾個禮拜心情、瞓覺、胃口點？
Now.rz: 佢開始出軌之後，我低落咗一個月。瞓得好差。
Now.r: Low for a month since he started cheating. Sleeping badly.

Background.t: Have you hurt yourself before? Any mental health care?
Background.tz: 你以前有冇傷害過自己？有冇睇過精神科？
Background.rz: 我後生嗰陣界過手。從來冇睇過精神科。
Background.r: I cut my arms as a teenager. Never seen a psychiatrist.
Background.mark: Asks about previous self-harm and psychiatric history

Background.r: I'd had a bottle of wine.

Background.t: Who can support you? What keeps you going?
Background.tz: 有邊個可以支持你？有咩令你撐落去？
Background.rz: 我家姐、我隻貓、我份工——我係老師。
Background.r: My sister, my cat, my job — I'm a teacher.

Background.t: Is anyone at home hurting you? Any children in your care?
Background.tz: 屋企有冇人傷害你？你有冇照顧緊小朋友？

steps.label: Agree a plan
steps.hint: Summarise, safety plan, involve her sister with consent, follow-up.

opts.t: It sounds like this was a very hard moment after the break-up, and you're feeling safer now. Before you go, can we make a safety plan together — warning signs, who to call, and keeping tablets away?
opts.tz: 聽落分手之後嗰一刻真係好難捱，而你而家覺得安全啲。走之前，我哋一齊做個安全計劃好唔好——有咩警號、搵邊個幫手，同埋將啲藥放遠啲？
opts.rz: 好。我可以俾家姐幫我保管啲藥。
opts.r: OK. My sister can keep my tablets.
opts.mark: Summarises and builds a safety plan with her

opts.t: Yes, your score is only 3, so you're low risk.
opts.tz: 可以，你個分數得三分，屬於低風險。

turns.line: OK. My sister can keep my tablets.
turns.lz: 好。我可以俾家姐幫我保管啲藥。

opts.t: Would it be OK for me to talk to your sister too? And I'll arrange a follow-up with the mental health team this week; here's the 24-hour crisis line.
opts.tz: 我可唔可以同你家姐都傾吓？我會安排精神健康團隊呢個禮拜跟進你；呢個係二十四小時危機熱線。
opts.mark: Involves family with consent and arranges follow-up

qs.q: NICE NG225 on risk scales like SAD PERSONS?
qs.a: Don't use them to predict risk or decide care
wrong: Admit anyone whose SAD PERSONS score is over 5

qs.a: Precautions against discovery and a final note
wrong: An impulsive act straight after an argument with a partner

qs.a: The 100-line on the nomogram from 4 hours
wrong: The 200-line on the nomogram, from 4 hours
Symptoms such as vomiting and RUQ pain alone

qs.a: Strong family support and reasons for living
Agreed warning signs, coping steps, contacts, safe means
wrong: A signed promise not to self-harm, kept by the GP and family
A numerical risk score to guide discharge
A discharge letter sent to the GP only

badge.name: Safe Plan
badge.flavor: Assess the person, not the score. Plan together, follow up.

options: A SAD PERSONS score to decide admission
Discharge once medically fit, no assessment
Not recommended; use a safety plan
Recommended for every patient before they leave

cards.q: Paracetamol overdose: NAC is given if the 4-hour level is…
options: Only if the ALT is raised
Should be avoided in the ED setting
cards.why: Direct questions are safe and necessary.

options: Treat with NAC regardless of level
Plot the 4-hour level on the treatment nomogram
Activated charcoal at 24 hours, then observe
cards.why: The nomogram is invalid for staggered doses.

options: Children in her care and domestic abuse
Her vaccination history as a child
